articles.title: Chamari Athapaththu’s 83 sinks Pakistan as Sri Lanka chase down 178 target to reach Asian Games final
articles.summary: Cricket News: Sri Lanka Women stormed into the gold-medal match of the Asian Games 2026 women’s cricket tournament after captain Chamari Athapaththu produced a matc.
articles.body: Sri Lanka Women stormed into the gold-medal match of the Asian Games 2026 women’s cricket tournament after captain Chamari Athapaththu produced a match-winning knock to guide her side to an eight-wicket victory over Pakistan in the first semi-final on Sunday.Chasing 178 at Korogi Sports Park, Sri Lanka reached 178/2 in 17.5 overs, sealing the win with 13 balls to spare. The victory guarantees Sri Lanka at least a silver medal, while Pakistan will compete in the bronze-medal match.Pakistan post competitive totalAfter a delayed start, Pakistan recovered from an early setback through a strong partnership between Ayesha Zafar and Shawaal Zulfiqar. Zafar led the charge with an aggressive 71 off 40 balls, while Zulfiqar contributed 54 off 50 deliveries. The pair added 115 runs to put Pakistan in a strong position before the team finished its 20 overs at 177/4.Athapaththu leads Sri Lanka’s emphatic chaseSri Lanka’s chase was anchored by Athapaththu, who struck an unbeaten 83 off 50 balls. Her innings featured seven boundaries and six sixes as she took control of the contest after settling in. Imesha Dulani added 26 off 21 balls, helping Sri Lanka maintain momentum, while the captain continued to attack the Pakistan bowlers and guide her team towards the target.Pakistan struggled to contain Sri Lanka, with their bowling and fielding unable to halt the scoring. Sri Lanka eventually completed the chase in 17.5 overs, losing just two wickets.The win sends Sri Lanka into the gold-medal match, where they will face the winner of the second semi-final between India and Bangladesh. Pakistan, meanwhile, will take on the losing side in the bronze-medal playoff.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Smriti Mandhana creates history in Asain Games semi-final, becomes leading run-scorer in Women's T20I
articles.summary: Cricket News: Smriti Mandhana made history in the Asian Games 2026 semi-final, becoming the highest run-scorer in women’s T20I cricket. The India opener achieved th.
articles.body: Smriti Mandhana made history in the Asian Games 2026 semi-final, becoming the highest run-scorer in women’s T20I cricket. The India opener achieved the milestones during a blistering start against Bangladesh, as India raced to 71/1 in the powerplay in their bid to book a place in the gold-medal match.India captain Harmanpreet Kaur won the toss and elected to bat first in the second semi-final. Mandhana and Shafali Verma provided an explosive start, putting Bangladesh’s bowlers under pressure from the outset.Mandhana surpasses Suzie BatesMandhana struck 37 off just 19 deliveries, hitting five fours and two sixes before her innings ended in the final over of the powerplay. She attempted another slog sweep off Nahida Akter but mistimed the shot, with Sobhana Mostary completing the catch at deep mid-wicket.Despite her dismissal, Mandhana had already etched her name in the record books, moving past New Zealand’s Suzie Bates to become the leading run-scorer in women’s T20Is. She also became the first Indian woman to reach 100 sixes in the format.Most runs in Women’s T20IsPlayerRunsSmriti Mandhana4,788Suzie Bates4,758Harmanpreet Kaur4,287Chamari Athapaththu4,282Sophie Devine3,817India make a flying startShafali joined Mandhana in attacking Bangladesh’s bowling, helping India reach 71/1 in the first six overs. The opening stand gave India early momentum in a high-stakes contest, with a place in the gold-medal match on the line.Playing XIs for India Women vs Bangladesh Women in the Asain Games Semi-finalIndia Women: Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Gunalan Kamalini, Harmanpreet Kaur (c), Richa Ghosh (wk), Bharti Fulmali, Deepti Sharma, Shreyanka Patil, Shree Charani, Nandani Sharma, Kranti Gaud.Bangladesh Women: Dilara Akter, Juairiya Ferdous, Sobhana Mostary, Nigar Sultana (wk/c), Shorna Akter, Sharmin Akhter, Shanjida Akter Meghla, Rabeya Khan, Nahida Akter, Marufa Akter, Sultana Khatun.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How one India T20I could become Japanese cricket's defining moment
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Alan Curr has stopped counting how many hats he's worn this week.On Sunday morning, with a typhoon on the horizon, the Japan Cricket Associ.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Alan Curr has stopped counting how many hats he's worn this week.On Sunday morning, with a typhoon on the horizon, the Japan Cricket Association (JCA) COO pulled covers off the wicket. Later, he was putting up hospitality tents, checking security plans and helping transform a quaint cricket ground with 500 permanent seats into a venue worthy of hosting the reigning T20I world champions. By Tuesday, weather permitting, India will walk out against Japan in the country's first-ever men's senior international against a Full Member.For Japanese cricket, getting here is success in itself and the scoreline almost secondary."A lot of success has almost already happened," Curr says. "The fact that India have agreed to come, the fact that I'm sitting here talking to you guys, the fact that Japanese media are coming to learn about cricket — we're having successes already," he told select media.Cricket is not new to Japan, having been introduced in the 1870s. But adaptation is a different story. Baseball, Football, Sumo Wrestling, Basketball, Golf, Tennis, Boxing are some sports that are bigger. India's arrival represents cricket's loudest introduction in recent memory.More than just another T20I matchJapan has played in Under-19 World Cups, faced India and Pakistan at youth level and competed in the Asian Games with its women's team. But this is different gravy."It certainly helps to say that the reigning world champions, the No. 1 ranked team in the world, are coming to Japan," Curr says. "It's piquing interest, but we've still got a long way to go before cricket breaks into the mainstream sporting audience."That mainstream audience is precisely what the JCA hopes to reach. The timing is ideal: cricket returns to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya just days later, allowing Japan to explain the sport through one of the country's most recognisable sporting events."The Asian Games gives cricket legitimacy that it didn't have before," Curr says. "You can't be what you can't see."It certainly helps to say that the reigning world champions, the No. 1 ranked team in the world, are coming to Japan.Cricket's quiet, but slow, growth in JapanBehind the scenes, cricket has been expanding steadily in Japan. Registered players have risen from around 3,000 when Curr arrived in 2014 to 8,800 today. The Japan Cup -- the T20 competition in the country -- has grown from barely a dozen teams to more than 80, while the domestic 40-over league now spans four divisions."Kaizen is the word," Curr says. "Continual improvement. That's what we're trying to do for the sport. But now and again there are moments like this where you can accelerate that," he added.Winning hearts and viewers, not necessarily the matchJapan harbour no illusions about the cricketing challenge ahead. "This India team is pretty good," Curr said as a matter of fact. "It's going to be an extremely difficult challenge for players who have never played at that level before."Instead, his measure of success is cultural.He points to Japan's women's team, praised recently for staying back after their Asian Games fixture against India to thank supporters and mingle with fans. That's the identity he wants the men's side to showcase too."We want cricket to be played hard but also be accessible and friendly," he says. "We want cricket to be fun."If thousands of first-time spectators leave Sano remembering more than just India's star power, Japanese cricket may have achieved exactly what it came for.The BCCI were really keen to have an opportunity to train. It's huge credit to them that they're excited about coming here and building this relationship with the JCAHow India fixture came into beingThe historic fixture was never part of Japan's grand plan to expand the sport. It began with clay.Eighteen months ago, the JCA set out to relay the turf square at Sano with help from Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC), whose groundsman travelled to Japan to identify suitable clay. The same surface was eventually used to build the Asian Games venue in Nagoya, prompting a simple thought: if Japan had international-quality wickets, why not invite the world's best teams to use them?Once the pitches were completed in March, Japan prepared a proposal and sent it to every Full Member ahead of the ICC conference in Edinburgh. Conversations with the BCCI began there — and, to Curr's surprise, moved quickly."The BCCI were really keen to have an opportunity to train. It's huge credit to them that they're excited about coming here and building this relationship with the JCA," he said.The timing made sense. With the Asian Games beginning days later, India men's squad would otherwise spend nearly a week waiting for their knockout fixture without access to proper cricket facilities. Sano offered both a training base and, eventually, a match. Again, with fingers crossed that the weather doesn't play spoilsport.India vs Japan T20I will be broadcast LIVE on FanCode on September 22 at 9:30 am IST.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: BCCI to draw line on Ombudsman’s jurisdiction over state-level matters | EXCLUSIVE
articles.summary: Cricket News: BENGALURU: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is set to introduce a policy defining the scope of the Ombudsman and preventing its office.
articles.body: BENGALURU: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) is set to introduce a policy defining the scope of the Ombudsman and preventing its office from entertaining complaints concerning local or state-level matters, the TimesofIndia.com has learnt.The move is understood to aim at drawing a clearer line between issues that fall within the Ombudsman’s jurisdiction and those that the respective state associations should address first. The move came after several members, including representatives of the Uttar Pradesh Cricket Association (UPCA), Kerala Cricket Association (KCA), Baroda Cricket Association (BCA), Punjab Cricket Association and Odisha Cricket Association (OCA), raised strong objections during the BCCI's Annual General Meeting (AGM) in Mumbai last week to the Ombudsman entertaining complaints related to local state matters.The members argued that such complaints lead to additional legal costs for the state associations and maintained that local grievance-redressal mechanisms should be exhausted before an issue is taken to the BCCI Ombudsman. They also questioned the Ombudsman's jurisdiction over matters that are primarily related to the functioning of individual state associations.Under the new framework, the Ombudsman will be provided with clear terms of reference governing the complaints it can entertain, particularly those relating to state associations."The BCCI will frame a policy that will curb the Ombudsman's interference in state-level matters. The board has decided to provide the Ombudsman with clear terms of reference when it comes to entertaining complaints related to state associations," an administrator who was part of the AGM told TimesofIndia.com.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: One-Day Cup final: Middlesex beat Leicestershire by 31 runs
articles.summary: Middlesex claim their first silverware in a decade as they beat Leicestershire in a thrilling One-Day Cup final.
articles.body:
Metro Bank Men's One-Day Cup final, Trent Bridge

Middlesex 231 (49.5 overs): Higgins 100, Duke 55; Holland 5-36

Leicestershire 200 (44.2 overs): Kelly 103; Roland-Jones 3-27, Helm 3-32

Middlesex claimed their first silverware in a decade as they fought back from a tricky start to beat Leicestershire in a thrilling One-Day Cup final at Trent Bridge.

Having been put into bat by Leicestershire captain Stephen Eskinazi, Ryan Higgins' magnificent hundred dug Middlesex out of a hole and helped them reach 231 before being bowled out in the final over of their innings.

Higgins, 31, struck nine fours in his 115-ball knock after his team had slumped to 71-5 in the 22nd over, putting on 135 with on-loan Yorkshire wicketkeeper Harry Duke (55) for the sixth wicket.

Ian Holland returned his second-best List-A figures of 5-36 for the Foxes, while England all-rounder Rehan Ahmed took 3-55.

In reply, Leicestershire too lost early wickets as former England seamer Toby Roland-Jones bowled 10 overs straight through in a fine opening spell of 3-27.

Leicestershire were indebted to the efforts of New Zealand international Nick Kelly, who reached a glorious century of his own off 103 deliveries and appeared to be taking his side to victory.

However, the game swung again in the over after Kelly reached his hundred as the left-hander heaved Tom Helm to Higgins on the mid-wicket fence to leave Leicestershire eight down.

And that proved the decisive moment as Helm dismissed Ajaz Patel and Tom Scriven skied Naavya Sharma straight up, with captain Ben Geddes taking the winning catch.

Middlesex's most recent success was the County Championship in 2016, and they had not won a white-ball trophy since lifting the T20 Blast in 2008.

Higgins & Roland-Jones star as Middlesex end drought

Middlesex had to overcome adversity more than once in Nottingham as they ended their long wait for a trophy.

They faced the most difficult batting conditions of the day in the opening hour and many teams would have crumbled at 71-5.

The sixth-wicket partnership between Higgins and Duke was a game-defining one as they fought back and gave their bowlers something to work with.

It was Higgins' first List-A hundred and it will live long in the memory for Middlesex supporters fortunate enough to watch it as he displayed character, graft and no shortage of skill.

Roland-Jones is a legendary figure at the club and he showed exactly why with a near-immaculate spell, taking the key scalps of Rishi Patel and Ahmed.

Sharma is Middlesex's leading wicket-taker in this competition and the 21-year-old too impressed with the ball, making the breakthrough as he found Eskinazi's outside edge, pinning Hamza Shaikh lbw and then returning to take the final wicket.

With Kelly in full flow, heads never went down and they showed all the composure of a team that have only lost once in this format all season.

Off the back of their 27-point deduction in the County Championship , Leicestershire's team talk is more than likely to have been straightforward.

And they started like a team with a point to prove after Eskinazi won the toss, backed by a vocal travelling support.

Holland set the tone with the new ball, nicking off Nathan Fernandes and Max Holden cheaply before Tom Scriven took two wickets of his own, including a fine catch by wicketkeeper Ben Cox to remove Josh De Caires (26).

Incredibly Cox caught the first five wickets to fall.

Middlesex fought back through Higgins and Duke, and the Foxes will perhaps look back on that partnership as an opportunity that slipped away.

Rishi Patel and Eskinazi got the chase off to a bright start, but three wickets for just three runs stalled their momentum and similarly to Middlesex's innings, Leicestershire found themselves five wickets down in the 70s.

Ahmed will regret his decision not to review after being given out lbw off Roland-Jones, with replays showing it would have missed leg stump.

Much as Higgins revived Middlesex, Kelly breathed new life into the Leicestershire chase with his defiant knock, which featured 10 fours and three sixes.

The Kiwi left-hander was being serenaded from the stands as the runs required ticked away, but he had to drag himself from the middle with 44 runs still needed.

Those fans continued to sing until the end, but were left disappointed as their team fell short.

articles.title: Ramesh Powar coaches Australia U-19 spinners ahead of India series
articles.summary: Cricket News: MUMBAI: Former India and Mumbai off-spinner Ramesh Powar is spending a few days with the Australian Under-19 team as a short-term coach for their spin.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Former India and Mumbai off-spinner Ramesh Powar is spending a few days with the Australian Under-19 team as a short-term coach for their spinners.Powar was present at the Australian junior team's nets at the Niranjan Shah Stadium in Rajkot on Sunday, giving some useful tips to Australia's young tweaker.“Cricket Australia had approached me quite a few months back to come and spend some time with their young spinners and guide them. I have previously also coached Australia’s spinners (he went in June 2018 on an invitation from CA to coach Australia’s under-23 spinners at CA's Centre of Excellence in Brisbane), so they have an idea of how I can help their young spinners. Since this was a prior commitment, I decided to spend four days with them,” Powar told TOI from Rajkot on Sunday.Powar joined the Australian team on Saturday and will be with the squad until its final Youth ODI against India on Wednesday. The first match of the Under-19 One-day series between India and Australia took place on Friday (India won by seven runs), with the next two matches slated for Monday and Wednesday.Powar has applied for the junior selector's post with the BCCI. The BCCI, however, is yet to conduct interviews for the position. Speaking to reporters after the Board’s AGM on Friday, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia had said that the candidates were being shortlisted, after which the Cricket Advisory Committee would interview them and complete the process over the next 15 days.A former India women's team head coach, Powar was the head coach of Gujarat for the last three seasons, and coached Mumbai to the Vijay Hazare Trophy title in March 2021.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Metro Bank One Day Cup men's final: Middlesex beat Leicestershire Foxes to end 36-year List A trophy wait
articles.summary: Ryan Higgins made a superb maiden List A hundred from 115 balls at Trent Bridge, playing a starring role as Middlesex ended a 36-year List A trophy drought by beating Leicestershire Foxes by 31 runs to win the Metro Bank One Day Cup in a low-scoring final
articles.body:
Ryan Higgins made a superb maiden List A hundred from 115 balls with Harry Duke (55) backing him up as their 135-run sixth-wicket partnership steered Middlesex from 71-5 to 231 all out after Foxes all-rounder Ian Holland took 5-36 and wicketkeeper Ben Cox held five catches. Higgins and Duke were making their first appearances for Middlesex in this year's competition.

New Zealand international batter Nick Kelly hit an equally brilliant 103 (107 balls) to lead a Leicestershire fightback from 79-5 but it was not enough to haul his side over the line, Tom Helm (3-32) claiming his vital wicket in a superb late spell as the Foxes were bowled out for 200.

In an impressive performance in the field by Middlesex, Toby Roland-Jones (3-27) showed his quality and 21-year-old pace prospect Naayva Sharma (3-37) finished as the competition's leading wicket-taker with 20.

Against a background of turmoil off the field, the win is a first for Middlesex in a List A final since they beat Derbyshire to lift the 1990 Refuge Assurance Cup.

Leicestershire, still reeling from the points deduction in the Rothesay County Championship that makes relegation almost certain, had hoped to ease the pain winning a second Metro Bank trophy in the space of four seasons but it was not to be.

Put in, Middlesex were 32-3 in the 11th over and five down in the 22nd - all snared by the immaculate Cox.

Nathan Fernandes slashed at one from Holland, who dismissed Max Holden in similar fashion, and Tom Scriven found a thin edge to remove skipper Ben Geddes for a duck.

Josh De Caires fell victim to a superb leg-side grab before Luke Hollman nicked a first-ball googly from Rehan Ahmed and Cox celebrated again.

But Duke - on loan from Yorkshire as cover for the injured Joe Cracknell - provided the support Higgins needed before a top edge to extra cover brought his undoing, Helm was leg before to Rehan and Higgins perished one ball after going to his maiden List A hundred, failing to clear long-on, looking for a 10th boundary.

The Leicestershire innings almost exactly mirrored that of Middlesex as they slipped to 32-3 and 79-5. Sharma dismissed Foxes captain and former Middlesex batter Stephen Eskinazi, caught at second slip, and Hamza Shaikh leg before, veteran Roland-Jones having Rishi Patel caught at deep square leg.

Roland-Jones claimed two more victims in Ahmed, leg before, and Cox, caught behind.

Leicestershire found themselves needing someone to step up as Higgins had and Kelly answered the call. Allowing few scoring opportunities to pass him by, reaching 50 from 52 balls with six fours and a pick-up for six off Sharma as he and Holland added 50 for the sixth wicket.

Ben Green's departure added more pressure, with 57 still needed. Kelly, who twice hammered Zafar down the ground for more sixes, kept the Foxes in the hunt, reaching 100 from 103 balls.

But, after needing treatment for cramp, he pulled Helm straight to deep square. Ajaz Patel fell to a stunning catch at backward point by Zafar off Helm, before Scriven was the last man to go, caught at mid-off.

articles.title: Gavin Williams dominates with 7 shutout frames as Guardians edge Athletics to stay atop AL Central
articles.summary: Gavin Williams threw seven shutout innings, Jo Adell had an RBI infield single and the Cleveland Guardians beat the Athletics 1-0 Sunday to remain atop the A...
articles.body:
CLEVELAND (AP) — Gavin Williams threw seven shutout innings, Jo Adell had an RBI infield single and the Cleveland Guardians beat the Athletics 1-0 Sunday to remain atop the AL Central.

Steven Kwan added three hits for Cleveland, which posted its seventh series sweep of the season and third at home.

The Guardians (81-75) are 1 1/2 games in front of the Chicago White Sox . They finish the season on the road with series against Boston and Kansas City .

Williams (14-8) gave up three hits and struck out nine to move into the major-league lead with 244 strikeouts. He has one more than Milwaukee 's Jacob Misiorowski . Toronto 's Dylan Cease is in third with 239. It is the 13th time in 31 starts this season that the right-hander has had at least nine strikeouts.

Cade Smith worked 1 1/3 innings for his 39th save in 44 opportunities.

The Athletics were swept for the second straight series and lost all six games on their road trip.

José Ramírez led off the fourth with a double down the right-field line, advanced to third on Chase DeLauter 's fly out to left and scored on Jo Adell's infield single. Pitcher Jack Perkins (3-12) fielded the soft grounder on the grass in front of the mound, but his throw hit Adell in the back as he was in the basepath.

Athletics manager Mark Kotsay was ejected for the third time this season for agruing the call.

Perkins went six innings and allowed one run on four hits.

The Athletics' best chance came in the eighth inning when they had runners on second and third with one out. Hunter Gaddis struck out pinch-hitter Carlos Cortes and Smith whiffed Henry Bolte.

Athletics: Return home to face the Los Angeles Angels on Tuesday. LHP Brady Brasso (1-3, 4.50 ERA) will take the mound.

Guardians: LHP Parker Messic (12-9, 2.57 ERA) goes on Tuesday to start a three-game series at Boston.

articles.title: Kade Anderson strong in Mariners 2-1 win in Colorado
articles.summary: Dominic Canzone picks up two key hits as Mariners extend season
articles.body:
Kade Anderson had his best-ever performance, and the Mariners extended their suffering another day.

The Mariners beat the Rockies 2-1 on Sunday in an uneventful game that was neither short nor long, exciting nor boring, meaningful nor insignificant. It was a baseball game between two bad teams, with just enough happening to be better than the offseason ahead. With the win, the Mariners take the series and avoid elimination entering the final week.

Anderson was the selling point for this one. He was fantastic for the first time in the majors. On the one hand, it came against the league's worst offense. On the other, it came at the league's launching pad in Denver. However you prefer to qualify it, Anderson was excellent in a Big League start that counts for real. He threw seven scoreless innings, allowed just three runs hits, and walked none while striking out seven. Most importantly, he got tons of chase out of the zone and picked up a career-high 14 whiffs:

It was good to see. Anderson struggle in his first five starts in the majors, with a 5.33 ERA and 4.44 FIP. He hadn't shown an ability to throw strikes or miss bats or prevent hard contact or keep the ball on the ground. That's not abnormal for a rookie, especially one who threw all of 93 innings in the minors and none above Double-A. But a strong outing Sunday — and hopefully one more against the Angels next week — is a nice confidence booster entering the offseason.

On the other side, the Mariners were getting perfecto'd through three innings, and I was getting a bit nervous that I'd need to put some effort into this recap. Thankfully, they figured out Tomoyuki Sugano in the fourth. Randy Arozarena drew an eight pitch walk, and Dominic Canzone singled up the middle to bring a hustling Arozarena around to score the game's first run. It looked like the Mariners might have a big inning in the works after Cal Raleigh walked, but Julio grounded into a double play to end the threat. The Mariners got a second run in the sixth inning, this time off Ryan Feltner . J.P Crawford singled to lead off, and Canzone doubled him home.

That was it for offense in this one. I'm not really exaggerating. I have listed three of the four hits and two of the three walks the Mariners collected in this one. Lazaro Montes walked in the seventh and Julio picked up an infield single in the ninth, if you want me to be thorough.

I was done with the recap, then Andrés Muñoz gave up a home run to Hunter Goodman in the bottom of the ninth to make it 2-1. After a walk, Dan Wilson came out with the trainer in tow. Muñoz left with an injury, and Eduard Bazardo took over. Bazardo struck out a batter, walked a batter to put the winning run on base, and struck out another batter to end the game.

The Mariners are still technically alive. The Rangers and Astros also lost on Sunday, so their "tragic number" remains at two. That puts the dagger in the hands of the Astros in Seattle next week.
